title: Book IV
coreMove: Convert opposition and complaint into material for reasoned action.
sourcePressure: The ruling part retreats inward, adapts to opposition like fire, examines complaint, and sees the world as a shared political community under change.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: obstacles are automatically good or retreat means escape

sourceAnchors.name: fire using what falls into it
sourceAnchors.detail: Book IV says the ruling part adapts to what is possible and uses opposition like fire using what falls into it.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The fire image matters because resistance becomes fuel only when purpose is already burning.

sourceAnchors.name: world as a political community
sourceAnchors.detail: Book IV argues from common reason to common law, fellow citizenship, and the world as a political community.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Inward retreat has to return to the world city, or it becomes only hiding.

counterintuition: what looks like control is actually surrender
the real problem is not outside you
tryThisNow: write down what you can control
examples: generic office meeting with laptop and coffee
parent-child bedtime conflict repeated across chapters

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: Megan rerouting crews after a track washout
exampleSpecs.stakes: complaint could consume the hour needed for a safe detour
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan circles the closed segment and turns the stranded crew into a bridge-inspection team.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The dispatch wall shows one red line cutting the route in half.

exampleSpecs.audience: Olivier losing the main dimmer before opening night
exampleSpecs.stakes: panic could make the production smaller than necessary
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivier rewrites the lighting cues around handheld lamps and makes the failure part of the staging.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The booth smells of hot dust when the dimmer rack goes black.

exampleSpecs.audience: Aanya facing a missing document on filing day
exampleSpecs.stakes: the missing paper could become blame instead of a new path
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya uses the missing certificate to build a sworn timeline and assign retrieval tasks before the client leaves.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We do not have the certificate," Aanya says, "so we start with the timeline."

exampleSpecs.audience: Henrik losing a sensor in rough water
exampleSpecs.stakes: the ruined instrument can still produce a usable observation window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What can a broken sensor still tell you if you stop asking it for the old data?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Henrik logs the failure time against tide movement and salvages a current pattern from the loss.

exampleSpecs.audience: Paula handling a party who refuses every proposal
exampleSpecs.stakes: opposition may reveal the only acceptable term
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Paula write down each refusal until the pattern shows the one nonnegotiable issue.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the mediator turn the word no into a map.

exampleSpecs.audience: James discovering a blocked fire exit during a supplier visit
exampleSpecs.stakes: embarrassment could lead to concealment instead of correction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 2:18 p.m., James stops the tour, moves the pallets, and turns the failed inspection into the first corrected standard.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 2:18 p.m., James sees the exit sign glowing over stacked pallets.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: convert obstacles without pretending they are pleasant
remove complaint by testing the opinion of harm

tryThisNowSpec: Take one obstruction in front of you and write the useful action it now makes possible, not the action it ruined.
